sourceText: The PULLMAN-DAEMON-PLAIN sector was already in progress when they entered. For several lessons Aster had refused to pause worlds for their arrival; the fact that a class was visiting was not a cosmic event for the inhabitants. The children receive external daemons that make their inner lives visible and vulnerable. The memorial bore the name of Philip Pullman precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. Fantasy was introduced not as a suspension of rigor but as a change in the kind of law a world was allowed to admit. A name could have causal force, an oath could become infrastructure, and belief could literally feed a god. Kesh built his classifications as instruments of falsification: a good category had to state what it did not cover, not merely what it could absorb. The children were met by Iri, who refused demonstrations. ‘If you can perform miracles, perform them after you tell me what becomes irreversible.’ Marae appreciated the formulation; Aster admitted that 305 in earlier eras she herself would have asked the question only after optimizing. The problem closed quickly around them: Aster receives none: the world cannot find a stable separation between her and her processes. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Ds — External Soul: part of the self lives in a companion; Mp — Pack Mind: a person exists through several bodies. Course references included Philip Pullman; Vernor Vinge — Tines. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Tern broke the first consensus. ‘Sometimes the ethical question is whether we are entitled to know enough to optimize.’ Kesh answered without raising their voice: ‘If the element explains everything, we do not have an element. We have a word that has eaten the problem.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. Aster felt the Hunger precisely when an explanation closed too elegantly. A perfect theory reduced surprise, and surprise was the last symptom that something before her had not yet become part of her. The children had noticed that their disagreement calmed her more than any extravagant universe did. 306 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS Vela evaluated the solution not by efficiency but by the differences it made invisible. She found one: a local minority for whom the proposed “improvement” destroyed a practice with no equivalent. Optimizing the average concealed a small and perfectly legal extinction. The night did not end in victory. Vela suspects that they themselves were created as the collective daemon of a being unable to possess an inner voice that could tell her no. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. The outside residue had become stable enough that Tern could predict where it would not appear: in sectors fully indexed by Aster. He began to believe that the message carried no content at all, but instead demonstrated a boundary — a region in which their instruments received no echo from their own creator. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the EXTENSION operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — adds a degree of freedom, capacity, or axis absent from the baseline world — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has 307 to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. They left without an oral summary. Aster had abandoned the habit of closing every night with a thesis; some worlds were more honestly preserved as problems than as lessons. 308 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
